detectorMechanism.guardReached: the HCM check is only reachable when `opened` is true, because qa-engine.js:224-227 returns early when !opened
detectorMechanism.defect: the second disjunct (`headText !== prevHead`) is a weak fallback intended for words whose popup headword legitimately differs from the surface (inflected form to lemma). It is ALSO satisfied by a completely DIFFERENT word’s popup, provided that word differs from the previous iteration’s headword. For these three nodes the popup never showed "Obgleich", yet `opened` evaluated true, so HCM compared Obgleich’s span colour against another word’s headword colour.
detectorMechanism.corroboration: no NO_POPUP finding fires on these nodes, which is only possible if `opened` was true — consistent with the fallback branch being taken rather than a genuine match
detectorMechanism.recordedHeadColour: rgb(245, 158, 11) = --g-adjective. Proven NOT to be Obgleich’s headword colour; the specific word it belonged to cannot be recovered from the baseline and is not claimed.

whyNotTheOtherClassifications.dataAuthoring: rejected as the HCM cause. There IS a separate authoring oddity here (see secondaryObservation), but the reported span/head colour comparison is invalid regardless of how the token is authored.
whyNotTheOtherClassifications.byDesign: rejected. The design permits an occurrence role to differ from a lexeme class; it does not permit comparing one word’s span against another word’s headword.
whyNotTheOtherClassifications.productionDefect: rejected for the colour rendering. The span colour is produced by exactly one canonical rule with no cascade conflict, and the popup side never rendered for this word at all — so no production rendering path produced a wrong colour.
whyNotTheOtherClassifications.unresolved: no longer applicable — the mechanism is now directly observed.

secondaryObservation.what: the three exercise chips render as r-object (auto-linkified guessRole) although the chapter authors "Obgleich" as r-conjunction / r-connector / r-konz elsewhere, and the exercise itself supplies roles: { Obgleich: r-konz }. A concessive conjunction shown in object green is pedagogically wrong under the colour-carries-meaning contract.
secondaryObservation.status: SEPARATE from the HCM verdict, and currently reported by NO detector
secondaryObservation.confidence: PROVEN (rendered class is r-object; authored roles are r-conjunction/r-connector/r-konz)
secondaryObservation.recommendedAction: curriculum/data review: have the sentence-ordering exercise apply its authored roles map to the rendered chips (or author the chips as tokens), so Obgleich renders with its concessive role rather than a guessed object role. NOT APPLIED.

recommendedAction.detector: tighten the HCM precondition so it requires a popup that actually belongs to the clicked word — i.e. gate HCM on headText matching the surface (or on a resolved-headword identity), not on the `headText !== prevHead` fallback. This is a QA-detector change, NOT a production change, and it is NOT APPLIED in this phase.
recommendedAction.expectedEffect: the 3 b2-15 findings would disappear; the other 34 HCM records are unaffected because their popups did resolve (they are `checked` occurrences with badge/role evidence available in 11 cases).
recommendedAction.caveat: before changing the detector, confirm on the other 34 that a stricter gate does not silently suppress genuine mismatches — several legitimately show a lemma headword that differs in spelling from the surface, which is exactly what the weak fallback was written to allow.
